paragraphs.sourceText: Extinction is a difficult concept to grasp. It is an 26 concept. It’s not at all like the killing of individual lifeforms that can be renewed through normal processes of reproduction. Nor is it simply 27 numbers. Nor is it damage that can somehow be remedied or for which some substitute can be found. Nor is it something that simply affects our own generation. Nor is it something that could be remedied by some supernatural power. It is rather an 28 and final act for which there is no remedy on earth or in heaven. A species once extinct is gone forever. However many generations 29 us in coming centuries, none of them will ever see this species that we extinguish.

Not only are we bringing about the extinction of life 30 , we are also making the land and the air and the sea so toxic that the very conditions of life are being destroyed. 31 basic natural resources, not only are the nonrenewable resources being 32 in a frenzy（疯狂）of processing, consuming, and 33 , but we are also ruining much of our renewable resources, such as the very soil itself on which terrestrial（地球上的）life depends.

The change that is taking place on the earth and in our minds is one of the greatest changes ever to take place in human affairs, perhaps the greatest, since what we are talking about is not simply another historical change or cultural 34 , but a change of geological and biological as well as psychological order of 35 .

paragraphs.sourceText: It seems to be a law in the technology industry that leading companies eventually lose their positions, often quickly and brutally. Mobile phone champion Nokia, one of Europe’s biggest technology success stories, was no 36 , losing its market share in just a few years.

In 2007, Nokia accounted for more than 40% of mobile phone sales 37 But consumers’ preferences were already 38 toward touch-screen smartphones. With the introduction of Applet iPhone in the middle of that year, Nokia’s market share 39 rapidly and revenue plunged. By the end of 2013, Nokia had sold its phone business to Microsoft.

What sealed Nokia’s fate was a series of decisions made by Stephen Elop in his position as CEO, which he 40 in October 2010. Each day that Elop spent in charge of Nokia, the company’s market value declined by $ 23 million, making him, by the numbers, one of the worst CEOs in history.

But Elop was not the only person at 41 Nokia’s board resisted change, making it impossible for the company to adapt to rapid shifts in the industry. Most 42 , Jorma Ollila, who had led Nokia’s transition from an industrial company to a technology giant, was too fascinated by the company’s 43 success to recognize the change that was needed to sustain its competitiveness.

The company also embarked on a 44 cost-cutting program, which included the elimination of thousands of jobs. This contributed to the 45 of the company’s once-spirited culture, which had motivated employees to take risks and make miracles. Good leaders left the company, taking Nokia’s sense of vision and directions with them. Not surprisingly, much of Nokia’s most valuable design and programming talent left as well. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。

paragraphs.sourceText: First-Generation College-Goers：Unprepared and Behind
paragraphs.translationZh: 第一代大学生：毫无准备且落后

paragraphs.sourceText: Kids who are the first in their families to brave the world of higher education come on campus with little academic know-how and are much more likely than their peers to drop out before graduation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 家庭中第一个勇敢进入高等教育世界的孩子在进入校园时几乎没有什么学术知识，而且比同龄人更有可能在毕业前辍学。

paragraphs.sourceText: A) When Nijay Williams entered college last fall as a first-generation student and Jamaican immigrant, he was academically unprepared for the rigors of higher education. Like many first-generation students, he enrolled in a medium-sized state university many of his high school peers were also attending, received a Pell Grant, and took out some small federal loans to cover other costs. Given the high price of room and board and the closeness of the school to his family, he chose to live at home and worked between 30 and 40 hours a week while taking a full class schedule.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）当尼杰·威廉姆斯（Nijay Williams）去年秋天作为第一代学生和牙买加移民进入大学时，他在学术上对高等教育的严格性没有做好准备。和许多第一代学生一样，他就读于一所中等规模的州立大学，他的许多高中同龄人也在就读，他获得了佩尔助学金，并申请了一些小额联邦贷款来支付其他费用。考虑到高昂的食宿费用以及学校与家人的距离，他选择住在家里，每周工作 30 至 40 小时，同时完成完整的课程安排。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) What Nijay didn’t realize about his school—Tennessee State University —was its frighteningly low graduation rate a mere 29 percent for its first-generation students. At the end of his first year, Nijay lost his Pell Grant of over $ 5 000 after narrowly missing the 2.0 GPA cut-off, making it impossible for him to continue paying for school.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) Nijay 没有意识到他的学校——田纳西州立大学——其第一代学生的毕业率低得惊人，仅为 29%。第一年结束时，Nijay 因 GPA 成绩仅差 2.0 的分数而失去了超过 5,000 美元的佩尔助学金，这使他无法继续支付学费。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Nijay represents a large and growing group of Americans：first-generation college students who enter school unprepared or behind. To make matters worse, these schools are ill-equipped to graduate these students—young adults who face specific challenges and obstacles. They typically carry financial burdens that outweigh those of their peers, are more likely to work while attending school, and often require significant academic remediation (补习）.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) Nijay 代表了一个庞大且不断增长的美国人群体：毫无准备或落后入学的第一代大学生。更糟糕的是，这些学校没有能力让这些面临特殊挑战和障碍的年轻人毕业。他们的经济负担通常比同龄人重，更有可能在上学期间工作，并且经常需要大量的学业补习。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Matt Rubinoff directs Tm First, a nonprofit organization launched last October to reach out to this specific population of students. He hopes to distribute this information and help prospective college- goers find the best post-secondary fit. And while Rubinoff believes there are a good number of four-year schools that truly care about these students and set aside significant resources and programs for them, he says that number isn’t high enough.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 马特·鲁宾诺夫 (Matt Rubinoff) 领导 Tm First，这是一个去年 10 月成立的非营利组织，旨在接触这一特定的学生群体。他希望传播这些信息并帮助未来的大学毕业生找到最适合的高等教育。尽管鲁比诺夫相信有很多四年制学校真正关心这些学生，并为他们预留了大量资源和项目，但他表示这个数字还不够高。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) “It’s not only the selective and elite institutions that provide those opportunities for a small subset of this population,” Rubinoff said, adding that a majority of first-generation undergraduates tend toward options such as online programs, two-year colleges, and commuter state schools. “Unfortunately, there tends to be a lack of information and support to help students think bigger and broader.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 鲁宾诺夫说：“为一小部分人提供这些机会的不仅仅是精英大学。”他补充说，大多数第一代本科生倾向于在线课程、两年制大学和通勤公立学校等选择。 “不幸的是，往往缺乏信息和支持来帮助学生进行更大更广泛的思考。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Despite this problem, many students are still drawn to these institutions—and two-year schools in particular. As a former high school teacher, I saw students choose familiar, cheaper options year after year. Instead of skipping out on higher education altogether, they chose community colleges or state schools with low bars for admittance.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 尽管存在这个问题，许多学生仍然被这些机构所吸引，尤其是两年制学校。作为一名前高中老师，我看到学生们年复一年地选择熟悉的、更便宜的选择。他们没有完全跳过高等教育，而是选择了入学门槛较低的社区大学或公立学校。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) “They underestimate themselves when selecting a university,” said Dave Jarrat, a marketing executive for Inside Track, a for-profit organization that specializes in coaching low-income students and supporting colleges in order to help students thrive. “The reality of it is that a lot of low-income kids could be going to elite universities on a full ride scholarship and don5t even realize it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) “他们在选择大学时低估了自己，”Inside Track 的营销主管戴夫·贾拉特 (Dave Jarrat) 说。Inside Track 是一家营利性组织，专门为低收入学生提供辅导并为大学提供支持，以帮助学生茁壮成长。 “现实情况是，许多低收入家庭的孩子可能会获得全额奖学金进入精英大学，但他们甚至没有意识到这一点。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) “Many students are coming from a situation where no one around them has the experience of successfully completing higher education, so they are coming in questioning themselves and their college worthiness,” Jarrat continued. That helps explain why, as I’m First’s Rubinoff indicated, the schools to which these students end up resorting can end up being some of the poorest matches for them. The University of Tennessee in Knoxville offers one example of this dilemma. A flagship university in the South, the school graduates just 16 percent of its first-generation students, despite its overall graduation rate of 71 percent. Located only a few hours apart, The University of Tennessee and Tennessee State are worth comparing. Tennessee State’s overall graduation rate is a tiny 39 percent, but at least it has a smaller gap between the outcomes for first-generation students and those of their peers.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) “许多学生的处境是，他们周围没有人有成功完成高等教育的经验，因此他们开始质疑自己和大学的价值，”贾拉特继续说道。这有助于解释为什么，正如 I’m First 的鲁比诺夫所说，这些学生最终就读的学校可能是最不适合他们的学校。位于诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学提供了这一困境的一个例子。该校是南方的旗舰大学，尽管总体毕业率为 71%，但第一代学生的毕业率仅为 16%。田纳西大学和田纳西州立大学距离仅几个小时，值得比较。田纳西州立大学的总体毕业率只有 39%，但至少第一代学生的成绩与同龄人之间的差距较小。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Still, the University of Tennessee deserves credit for being transparent. Many large institutions keep this kind of data secret—or at least make it incredibly difficult to find. The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, for instance, admits only that the graduation rate for its first-generation pupils is “much lower” than the percentage of all students who graduate within four years (81 percent).
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 尽管如此，田纳西大学的透明度还是值得赞扬的。许多大型机构对此类数据保密，或者至少使其难以找到。例如，北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校仅承认其第一代学生的毕业率“远低于”四年内毕业的所有学生的比例（81%）。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) It is actually quite difficult to find reliable statistics on the issue for many schools. Higher education institutions are, under federal law, required to report graduation rates, but these reports typically only include Pell recipient numbers—not necessarily rates specific to first-generation students. Other initiatives fail to break down the data, too. Imagine how intimidating it can be for prospective students unfamiliar with the complexities of higher education to navigate this kind of information and then identify which schools are the best fit.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 对于许多学校来说，实际上很难找到关于这个问题的可靠统计数据。根据联邦法律，高等教育机构必须报告毕业率，但这些报告通常只包括佩尔奖获得者的人数，不一定是针对第一代学生的毕业率。其他举措也未能分解数据。想象一下，对于不熟悉高等教育复杂性的未来学生来说，浏览此类信息并确定哪些学校最适合是多么令人生畏。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) It was this lack of information that prompted the launch of Tm First in 2013, originally as an arm of its umbrella organization, the Center For Student Opportunity. “If we can help to direct students to more of these types of campuses and help students to understand them to be realistic and accessible places, have them apply to these schools at greater frequency and ultimately get in and enroll, we are going to raise the success rate,” Rubinoff said, citing a variety of colleges ranging from large state institutions to smaller private schools.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 正是信息的缺乏促使 Tm First 在 2013 年成立，最初是作为其伞式组织学生机会中心的一个分支。鲁比诺夫说：“如果我们能够帮助引导学生进入更多此类校园，并帮助学生了解它们是现实且方便的地方，让他们更频繁地申请这些学校并最终进入并注册，我们将提高成功率。”他列举了从大型公立学校到小型私立学校的各种大学。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Chelsea Jones, who now directs student programming at I’m First, was a first-generation college student at Howard. Like other student new to the intimidating higher-education world, she often struggled on her path to college, “There wasn’t really a college-bound culture at my high school,” she said. “I wanted to go to college but I didn’t really know the process.” Jones became involved with a college-access program through Princeton University in high school. Now, she attributes much of her understanding of college to that：“But once I got to campus, it was a completely different ball game that no one really prepared me for.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) Chelsea Jones 是霍华德学院的第一代大学生，她现在负责 I'm First 的学生项目。和其他刚进入令人生畏的高等教育世界的学生一样，她在上大学的道路上经常遇到困难，“我的高中并没有真正的大学文化，”她说。 “我想上大学，但我不太了解这个过程。”琼斯在高中时参与了普林斯顿大学的大学入学计划。现在，她将自己对大学的理解很大程度上归因于这一点：“但一旦我进入校园，这是一场完全不同的球赛，没有人真正为我做好准备。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) She was fortunate, though. Howard, a well-regarded historically black college, had an array of resources for its first-generation students, including matching kids with counselors, connecting first- generation students to one another, and TRIO, a national program that supported 200 students on Howard’s campus. Still, Jones represents a small percentage of first-generation students who are able to gain entry into more elite universities, which are often known for robust financial aid packages and remarkably high graduation rates for first-generation students. (Harvard, for example, boasts a six- year graduation rate for underrepresented minority groups of 98 percent.)
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 不过她很幸运。霍华德大学是一所享有盛誉的历史悠久的黑人大学，为第一代学生提供了一系列资源，包括为孩子匹配辅导员、将第一代学生彼此联系起来，以及 TRIO（一项为霍华德校园的 200 名学生提供支持的国家计划）。尽管如此，琼斯在能够进入更多精英大学的第一代学生中只占一小部分，这些大学通常以强大的经济援助计划和第一代学生极高的毕业率而闻名。 （例如，哈佛就拥有 98% 的少数族裔六年毕业率。）

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Christian Vazquez, a first-generation Yale graduate, is another exception, his success story setting him far apart from students such as Nijay. “There is a lot of support at Yale, to an extent, after a while, there is too much support,” he said, half-joking about the countless resources available at the school. Students are placed in small groups with counselors (trained seniors on campus); they have access to cultural and ethnic affinity (联系）groups, tutoring centers and also have a summer orientation specifically for first-generation students (the latter being one of the most common programs for students).
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 第一代耶鲁大学毕业生克里斯蒂安·巴斯克斯 (Christian Vazquez) 是另一个例外，他的成功故事使他与尼杰 (Nijay) 等学生相距甚远。 “耶鲁大学提供了很多支持，在某种程度上，过了一段时间，支持就太多了，”他半开玩笑地谈到学校拥有的无数资源。学生被分成小组，有辅导员（校园内经过培训的高年级学生）；他们可以接触文化和种族亲和力的团体、辅导中心，还可以参加专门针对第一代学生的夏季迎新活动（后者是学生最常见的项目之一）。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) “Our support structure was more like: ‘You are going to get through Yale; you are going to do well,’” he said, hinting at mentors (导师）, staff, and professors who all provided significant support for students who lacked confidence about “belonging” at such a top institution.
paragraphs.translationZh: O）“我们的支持结构更像是：‘你会通过耶鲁大学；你会做得很好，’”他说，暗示着导师（导师）、工作人员和教授，他们都为那些对这样一个顶级机构的“归属感”缺乏信心的学生提供了重要的支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Many first-generation college-goers have doubts about their abilities to get a college degree.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 许多第一代大学生对自己获得大学学位的能力表示怀疑。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. First-generation college students tend to have much heavier financial burdens than their peers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 第一代大学生往往比同龄人承受更重的经济负担。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. The graduation rate of first-generation students at Nijay’s university was incredibly low.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. Nijay 大学第一代学生的毕业率极低。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Some top institutions like Yale seem to provide first-generation students with more support than they actually need.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 像耶鲁大学这样的一些顶尖院校似乎为第一代学生提供了比他们实际需要的更多的支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. On entering college, Nijay Williams had no idea how challenging college education was.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 进入大学后，尼杰·威廉姆斯并不知道大学教育有多么具有挑战性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Many universities simply refuse to release their exact graduation rates for first-generation students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 许多大学干脆拒绝公布第一代学生的确切毕业率。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. According to a marketing executive, many students from low-income families don’t know they could have a chance of going to an elite university.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 据一位营销主管称，许多来自低收入家庭的学生不知道他们有机会进入精英大学。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Some elite universities attach great importance to building up the first-generation students, self-confidence.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Saying they can no longer ignore the rising prices of health care, some of the most influential medical groups in the nation are recommending that doctors weigh the costs, not just the effectiveness of treatments, as they make decisions about patient care.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国一些最有影响力的医疗团体表示，他们不能再忽视医疗保健价格的上涨，他们建议医生在做出患者护理决定时权衡成本，而不仅仅是治疗的有效性。

paragraphs.sourceText: The shift, little noticed outside the medical establishment but already controversial inside it, suggests that doctors are starting to redefine their roles, from being concerned exclusively about individual patients to exerting influence on how healthcare dollars are spent.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种转变在医疗机构之外很少引起注意，但在医疗机构内部已经引起争议，这表明医生开始重新定义自己的角色，从只关心个别患者转变为对医疗保健费用的支出施加影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: In practical terms, the new guidelines being developed could result in doctors choosing one drug over another for cost reasons or even deciding that a particular treatment—at the end of life, for example—is too expensive. In the extreme, some critics have said that making treatment decisions based on cost is a form of rationing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 实际上，正在制定的新指南可能会导致医生出于成本原因选择一种药物而不是另一种药物，甚至认为某种特定的治疗（例如在生命的尽头）过于昂贵。一些批评家极端地表示，根据成本做出治疗决定是一种配给形式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Traditionally, guidelines have heavily influenced the practice of medicine, and the latest ones are expected to make doctors more conscious of the economic consequences of their decisions, even though there’s no obligation to follow them. Medical society guidelines are also used by insurance companies to help determine reimbursement（报销）policies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 传统上，指南对医学实践产生了重大影响，而最新的指南预计将使医生更加意识到其决定的经济后果，尽管没有义务遵守它们。保险公司也使用医学会指南来帮助确定报销政策。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some doctors see a potential conflict in trying to be both providers of patient care and financial overseers. “There should be forces in society who should be concerned about the budget, but they shouldn’t be functioning simultaneously as doctors,” said Dr. Martin Samuels at a Boston hospital. He said doctors risked losing the trust of patients if they told patients, “I’m not going to do what I think is best for you because I think it’s bad for the healthcare budget in Massachusetts.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些医生认为，试图同时充当患者护理提供者和财务监督者可能存在冲突。波士顿一家医院的马丁·塞缪尔斯博士说：“社会上应该有一些力量关心预算，但他们不应该同时充当医生。”他说，如果医生告诉患者，“我不会做我认为对你最好的事情，因为我认为这对马萨诸塞州的医疗预算不利，那么他们就有失去患者信任的风险。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Doctors can face some grim trade-offs. Studies have shown, for example, that two drugs are about equally effective in treating macular degeneration, and eye disease. But one costs $ 50 a dose and the other close to $ 2 000. Medicare could save hundreds of millions of dollars a year if everyone used the cheaper drug, Avastin, instead of the costlier one, Lucentis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 医生可能面临一些严峻的权衡。例如，研究表明，两种药物在治疗黄斑变性和眼病方面的效果大致相同。但其中一种的价格为每剂 50 美元，另一种则接近 2,000 美元。如果每个人都使用更便宜的药物阿瓦斯汀 (Avastin)，而不是更昂贵的药物雷珠单抗 (Lucentis)，医疗保险每年可以节省数亿美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the Food and Drug Administration has not approved Avastin for use in the eye, and using it rather than the alternative, Lucentis, might carry an additional, although slight, safety risk. Should doctors consider Medicare’s budget in deciding what to use?
paragraphs.translationZh: 但美国食品和药物管理局尚未批准阿瓦斯汀用于眼部，使用它而不是替代品雷珠单抗可能会带来额外的（尽管轻微的）安全风险。医生在决定使用什么药物时是否应该考虑医疗保险的预算？

paragraphs.sourceText: “I think ethically(在道德层面上）we are just worried about the patient in front of us and not trying to save money for the insurance industry or society as a whole,” said Dr. Donald Jensen.
paragraphs.translationZh: “我认为从道德角度来说，我们只是担心我们面前的病人，而不是试图为保险业或整个社会省钱，”唐纳德·詹森博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Still, some analysts say that there’s a role for doctors to play in cost analysis because not many others are doing so. “In some ways,” said Dr. Daniel Sulmasy, “it represents a failure of wider society to take up the issue.” 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管如此，一些分析师表示，医生在成本分析中可以发挥作用，因为没有多少其他人这样做。 “在某些方面，”丹尼尔·苏尔马西博士说，“这代表了更广泛的社会未能解决这个问题。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Economic inequality is the “defining challenge of our time,” President Barack Obama declared in a speech last month to the
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国总统巴拉克·奥巴马 (Barack Obama) 上个月在一次演讲中宣称，经济不平等是“我们这个时代的决定性挑战”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Center for American Progress. Inequality is dangerous, he argued, not merely because it doesn’t look good to have a large gap between the rich and the poor, but because inequality itself destroys upward mobility, making it harder for the poor to escape from poverty. “Increased inequality and decreasing mobility pose a fundamental threat to the American Dream,” he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国进步中心。他认为，不平等是危险的，不仅因为贫富差距过大看起来不太好，还因为不平等本身破坏了向上流动性，使穷人更难摆脱贫困。 “不平等的加剧和流动性的下降对美国梦构成了根本威胁，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Obama is only the most prominent public figure to declare inequality Public Enemy No. 1 and the greatest threat to reducing poverty in America. A number of prominent economists have also argued that it’s harder for the poor to climb the economic ladder today because the rungs (横档）in that ladder have grown farther apart.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奥巴马是宣布不平等为第一号公敌以及美国减贫面临的最大威胁的最著名的公众人物。许多著名的经济学家也认为，今天的穷人攀登经济阶梯变得更加困难，因为阶梯上的横档已经变得越来越远。

paragraphs.sourceText: For all the new attention devoted to the 1 percent, a new dataset from the Equality of Opportunity Project at Harvard and Berkeley suggests that, if we care about upward mobility overall, we’re vastly exaggerating the dangers of the rich-poor gap. Inequality itself is not a particularly strong predictor of economic mobility, as sociologist Scott Winship noted in a recent article based on his analysis of this data.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管新的注意力集中在 1% 的人身上，但哈佛和伯克利机会均等项目的一个新数据集表明，如果我们关心整体的向上流动性，我们就大大夸大了贫富差距的危险。正如社会学家斯科特·温希普（Scott Winship）在最近基于对这些数据的分析的文章中指出的那样，不平等本身并不是经济流动性的特别有力的预测因素。

paragraphs.sourceText: So what factors, at the community level, do predict if poor children will move up the economic ladder as adults? What explains, for instance, why the Salt Lake City metro area is one of the 100 largest metropolitan areas most likely to lift the fortunes of the poor and the Atlanta metro area is one of the least likely?
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，在社区层面，哪些因素可以预测贫困儿童成年后是否会在经济阶梯上升级呢？例如，为什么盐湖城都市区是最有可能提高穷人财富的 100 个最大都市区之一，而亚特兰大都市区却是最不可能的之一？

paragraphs.sourceText: Harvard economist Raj Chetty has pointed to economic and racial segregation, community density, the size of a community’s middle class, the quality of schools, community religiosity, and family structure, which he calls the “single strongest correlate of upward mobility.” Chetty finds that communities like Salt Lake City, with high levels of two-parent families and religiosity, are much more likely to see poor children get ahead than communities like Atlanta, with high levels of racial and economic segregation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈佛大学经济学家拉杰·切蒂指出，经济和种族隔离、社区密度、社区中产阶级的规模、学校质量、社区宗教信仰和家庭结构，他称之为“向上流动的唯一最强相关因素”。切蒂发现，像盐湖城这样的双亲家庭和宗教信仰程度较高的社区，比亚特兰大这样的种族和经济隔离程度较高的社区更有可能看到贫困儿童取得成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: Chetty has not yet issued a comprehensive analysis of the relative predictive power of each of these factors. Based on my analyses of the data, of the factors that Chetty has highlighted, the following three seem to be most predictive of upward mobility in a given community：
paragraphs.translationZh: 切蒂尚未对这些因素的相对预测能力进行全面分析。根据我对数据的分析，在切蒂强调的因素中，以下三个因素似乎最能预测特定社区的向上流动：

paragraphs.sourceText: 1. Per-capita（人均）income growth
paragraphs.translationZh: 1. 人均收入增长

paragraphs.sourceText: 2. Prevalence of single mothers (where correlation is strong, but negative)
paragraphs.translationZh: 2. 单身母亲的患病率（相关性很强，但呈负相关）

paragraphs.sourceText: 3. Per-capita local government spending
paragraphs.translationZh: 3、地方政府人均支出

paragraphs.sourceText: In other words, communities with high levels of per-capita income growth, high percentages of two-parent families, and high local government spending—which may stand for good schools —are the most likely to help poor children relive Horatio Alger5s rags-to-riches story. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 换句话说，人均收入增长水平高、双亲家庭比例高、地方政府支出高（这可能代表着好学校）的社区最有可能帮助贫困儿童重温霍雷肖·阿尔杰（Horatio Alger）白手起家的故事。
